record.context_brief: positivity forced by nontrivial group actions
record.original_question: Conjecture: if a manifold M admits a nontrivial action by a Lie group G, then M carries a metric with a corresponding positivity property; for example, if k = dim G and λ_1, ..., λ_k are Ricci-curvature eigenvalues, then λ_1 + ··· + λ_k ≥ 0.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.11. If \(M\) admits a nontrivial \(G\)-action, then it carries a metric with certain positivity. For instance, if \(k=\dim G\), then \(\lambda_1+\dots+\lambda_k\geq 0\) where \(\lambda_j\) are the eigenvalues of the Ricci curvature.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth closed manifold and let $G$ be a Lie group of dimension $k \geq 1$ that acts smoothly and nontrivially on $M$. Prove or disprove the following: $M$ admits a Riemannian metric $g$ such that, at every point $p \in M$, the eigenvalues $\lambda_1(p) \leq \lambda_2(p) \leq \cdots \leq \lambda_n(p)$ of the Ricci curvature tensor of $g$ (with $n = \dim M$) satisfy
$$\lambda_1(p) + \lambda_2(p) + \cdots + \lambda_k(p) \geq 0.$$
That is, every manifold admitting a nontrivial Lie group action of dimension $k$ carries a metric whose Ricci tensor is $k$-nonnegative (the sum of any $k$ eigenvalues — equivalently, the smallest $k$ — is nonnegative).
artifact.category_tag: k-positive Ricci curvature and group actions
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any specific resolution of this conjecture relating nontrivial Lie group actions on a manifold to the existence of a metric with $k$-nonnegative Ricci curvature (sum of the $k$ smallest Ricci eigenvalues nonnegative, where $k = \dim G$). Related work on $k$-positive Ricci curvature (e.g., Wolfson) exists but does not appear to settle this statement. Status is therefore unknown from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Manifolds with k-positive Ricci curvature (J. Wolfson)
status_evidence.snippet: A manifold M has k-positive Ricci curvature if at each point the sum of the k smallest eigenvalues of the Ricci curvature is positive.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of k-positive Ricci curvature appearing in the conjecture is studied in the literature, but no proof or disproof of the stated conjecture for nontrivial Lie group actions was found.
